text.official_en: Rrrgh...!

text.jp:
……我々も手を尽くしておりますので、
どうかここはお任せください……！
text.official_en: We are doing everything in our power to bring the situation under control. Leave this to us!

text.jp:
あの娘、不思議そうな顔してたな……
完全に変な奴だ俺……。
text.official_en: She gave me the strangest look, like I was absolutely out of my mind.

text.jp:
あの花はな、
ここでしか咲かないってこともないんだが……
光を放つのは、オルデリオンだけらしいぞ。
text.official_en: You can find similar flowers elsewhere, but apparently they only glow here in Olderion.

text.jp: あれは、なんだったのかしら？
text.official_en: What in the world was he on about?

text.jp:
いえ。こんなときこそ、自分たちの力で
どうにかしないといけないのかもしれませんね。
text.official_en: ...No. It’s precisely at times like these that we must focus on what we can do for ourselves.

text.jp:
いつこちら側に魔物が現れても逃げられるよう
住民の避難の準備を進めているんだ。
text.official_en: We’re preparing to evacuate the residents in the event that monsters show up here as well.

text.jp:
いまは飛空艇の勢いに押されちゃいるが
昔はこの国の海運業が
世界の物の流れの中心だったんだよ。
text.official_en: Airships are more popular these days, but there was a time when our ships used to transport people all around the world.
text.real_en: Airships may have overtaken them now, but our maritime trade used to be at the heart of the world's flow of goods.

text.jp:
うちの孫娘とそんなに歳も
変わらないのに立派なことじゃ。
ありがたや　ありがたや。
text.official_en: Can you believe that she is almost as young as my granddaughter? To take on such a heavy burden at that age... Praise be to her resilience.

text.jp:
おかげで俺たちの仕事は
簡単な警備が主なのさ。
text.official_en: So there is little for us guards to do, other than keep an eye on things.
text.real_en: Thanks to that, our work mostly consists of routine patrols.

text.jp:
ここは、全船乗り憧れの街なんだ。
帰る前に隅々まで目に焼き付けるぞ……！
text.official_en: There isn’t a sailor alive who doesn’t dream of this place. I want to see every last bit of it before I return home!

text.jp: ここは、水と花の都オルデリオン。
text.official_en: This is Olderion, city of water and blossoms.

text.jp: ここを通してくれ！
text.official_en: Let me through!

text.jp: こちらに水が来るのも時間の問題か……？
text.official_en: Is it only a matter of time before the water reaches here as well?

text.jp:
こちら側に避難していたおかげで
洪水には巻き込まれずに済んだんだ。
text.official_en: We had already evacuated over here, so thankfully we didn’t get caught in the flood.

text.jp:
こっちにも水が来る前に
早く逃げた方がいいのかな……？
text.official_en: Maybe I should get out of here before the water reaches this area, too?

text.jp:
この先の旧市街は危険です！
一般の方を通すわけにはいきません。
text.official_en: It’s too dangerous to go to Old Town right now! For your own safety, I cannot allow civilians to pass.

text.jp:
この先の旧市街は現在、
複数の魔物の襲撃を受けています……。
text.official_en: Old Town lies beyond this point, but it is currently beset by monsters.

text.jp:
この国には水の守り人という
代々オルデリオンの水を守る一族がおってな。
text.official_en: The group known as the Wardens of the Waters has protected Olderion and its waters for generations.
text.real_en: There's a family known as the Wardens of Water. They've protected Olderion's waters for generations.

text.jp:
この美しい花たちも
水に沈んで流されてしまうのだろうか……。
text.official_en: Will all these gorgeous flowers be washed away, too?

text.jp:
この街の移動には、渡し舟が便利だよ。
乗っていくかい？
text.official_en: The easiest way to get around the city is by gondola. So, how about a ride?

text.jp:
この街の美しさは今日も変わらない……
あの人がいないままなのに……。
text.official_en: The city is as beautiful as ever, even though my love graces it no longer...
text.real_en: This city is just as beautiful as ever... even with that person still gone...

text.jp:
この街を守るのは、水の加護だけじゃない。
俺たちなんだ。頑張るよ。
text.official_en: It’s not just the protective power of the water that guards this city. Those of us who call it home must keep it safe as well.

text.jp: これですべて元通り、となれば良いが……。
text.official_en: I hope everything will go back to normal now.

text.jp: これ以上、酷くならないことを祈るばかりだよ。
text.official_en: I’ve been praying that things don’t get any worse than they already are.

text.jp:
こんなことが起きるなんて
想像したこともなかったんだよ……。
text.official_en: I never imagined anything like this would happen here...

text.jp:
そういえば、旧市街の方が騒がしいけど
何かあったのかな？
text.official_en: Speaking of which, I heard a lot of noise coming from Old Town. Is everything all right over there?

text.jp:
その中でも水神様と心を交わせる者が
水の巫女と呼ばれるのじゃ。
text.official_en: Amongst them is a Water Maiden, who they say can join her very heart and mind with the God of Water.
text.real_en:
Among them, those who can commune
with the God of Water are called Water Maidens.

text.jp:
そりゃなかなか難しいかもしれん。
水の巫女は水の洞窟で
民のために毎日祈りを捧げてるからのう。
text.official_en: Ah, that might prove to be difficult. The Maiden prays at the Cave of Waters daily as a part of her duty to the people, you see.

text.jp:
それほどまでに
オルデリオンの加護を頼り過ぎていたんだな。
text.official_en: I guess we’ve been too dependent on Olderion’s protection for too long.

text.jp:
でも、何故かしらね。
これで前に進めそうな気もするの。
text.official_en: And yet, for some reason, I feel as though I can finally move forward.

text.jp: どうか慌てず、避難誘導に従ってください。
text.official_en: Please remain calm and evacuate as you are directed.

text.jp:
どうだい美味しいだろう？
オルデリオンでとれたばかりの
新鮮なお魚だからねぇ。
text.official_en: You like that, don’t you, dear? It was freshly caught here in Olderion, after all.

text.jp: な、なんて美しいんだ……。
text.official_en: It’s breathtaking...

text.jp:
へえ。
会ってみたいな。水の巫女に。
text.official_en: Wow, she sounds like one brave girl. I’d like to meet her if I have the chance.
text.real_en: Oh, I'd like to meet the Water Maiden.

text.jp:
まぁ、この国はいつも通り
中立の立場をとるだろうがな。
text.official_en: Well, even if there is, we’ll probably just stay neutral, as always.

text.jp:
まるで戦艦のような飛空艇が飛んで行ったが……
どこかで戦争でも起きないといいなぁ……。
text.official_en: An airship that seemed armed for battle just flew by. I hope there isn’t a war brewing somewhere...
text.real_en: An airship that looked like a battleship just flew by... I hope there isn't a war brewing somewhere...

text.jp:
もう他のお魚じゃ満足できないねぇ。
フッフッフッ。
text.official_en: Once you’ve tasted the seafood here, nothing else will do!

text.jp:
ようやく一段落したよ。
まだまだ仕事は山積みだけどね。
text.official_en: Things have finally settled down some, but there is still plenty of work to be done.

text.jp:
んん？
あそこの水面が一瞬光ったような……？
text.official_en: Is it just me, or did the water shimmer for a second there?

text.jp:
オルデリオンって
新鮮な魚が名産だって思われがちなんだけどさ。
text.official_en: Many outsiders assume that fishing is Olderion’s main industry.
text.real_en: People tend to think Olderion is famous only for its fresh fish.

text.jp:
オルデリオンに流れる水は
この街を守護する力を持っているんだ。
text.official_en: The waters that flow through Olderion have a special property that protects the aquapolis.

text.jp:
オルデリオンの水は
水の守り人が特別な力で
清らかに保っているんだよ。
text.official_en: The Wardens of the Waters have long used their special powers to keep Olderion’s water pure.
text.real_en: The Warden of Water keeps Olderion's water pure through a special power.

text.jp:
キラキラ光っている花が
水の上に咲いているだろう？
text.official_en: Do you see those glittering flowers blooming on the water’s surface?

text.jp:
グランポートの水路には
この国の技術がタダで提供されているんだぜ。
text.official_en: We helped construct Grandport’s canals free of charge.
text.real_en: Olderion provided the technology for Grandport's canals free of charge.

text.jp:
一族相伝の力だから
誰でも使えるわけじゃないんだってさ。
text.official_en: Their power is hereditary. Not just anyone can use it.

text.jp: 俺、泳げないんだ……。
text.official_en: Believe it or not...I can’t swim!

text.jp:
口から水を吐くこの像は
水神様を模しているんです。
text.official_en: This statue depicts the God of Water.
text.real_en:
That statue with water flowing from its mouth
depicts the God of Water.

text.jp:
君がふと旅を振り返ったとき……
この街での思い出が、美しいものであることを祈ろう。
text.official_en: I pray that when you look back on your journey one day, you’ll have only the fondest memories of our home.

text.jp: 守り人様の手を煩わせるわけにはいきませんから！
text.official_en: We cannot allow the Wardens to trouble themselves with such details!
text.real_en: We can't put the Warden to any more trouble!

text.jp:
店内がきれいだと、居心地が良くて
ついつい買い過ぎちゃうのよねぇ。
text.official_en: A clean and uncluttered shop makes customers want to stay longer and buy more!

text.jp: 心なしか花の元気もないように見える……。
text.official_en: Somehow even the flowers seem to have lost their vitality.

text.jp: 息子がまだ、取り残されているかもしれないんだ！
text.official_en: But my son might still be there!

text.jp:
悔しいですが、我々だけでは
事態を収束できずにいます。
どうか、お力添えください……！
text.official_en: Though it pains me to admit it, we cannot deal with them on our own. Please, lend us your aid!

text.jp:
新市街は水路が整備されているとはいえ
それもいつまで持つか……。
text.official_en: New Town was built with canals that can carry some of the water away, but I wonder how long they will hold?

text.jp:
旧市街の方が騒がしいな……。
何があったんだ……？
text.official_en: I heard a lot of noise coming from Old Town. Is something the matter?

text.jp:
早くご自身の家に帰れるように
これからも我々は尽力してまいります！
text.official_en: But we will do everything within our power to see them returned to their own homes as quickly as possible!

text.jp:
本来は成人してから継承の儀を行うのじゃが、
数年前に母親が病気で亡くなってしまってのう。
ずいぶんと早く大任に就くことになったのじゃ。
text.official_en: Normally, a rite of succession grants the Water Maiden her position <text style="italic">after</> reaching adulthood...but since illness took her mother, the poor girl’s borne the responsibility from a young age.
text.real_en: Normally, the Water Maiden undergoes the rite of succession <text style="italic">after</> reaching adulthood... But her mother died of an illness a few years ago, so she had to take on that responsibility much earlier than usual.

text.jp:
橋の上のあの娘……
今日も海を眺めてるな……。
text.official_en: That girl atop the bridge is gazing out to sea again today.

text.jp:
橋の上のあの娘にもう一度、
話しかけるべきか……
話しかけないべきか……。
text.official_en: I don’t know... Should I talk to the girl on the bridge again or not?

text.jp:
気のせいかもしれないが
なんだかいいことがありそうな気がするぞ。
text.official_en: Maybe I’m just seeing things, but I get the feeling there might be something there.
text.real_en: Maybe I imagined it, but I have a feeling something good is going to happen.

text.jp:
水の巫女は継承制でのう。
今は末っ子が受け継いでおる。
text.official_en: The position of the Water Maiden is passed down from generation to generation. The youngest of the Wardens currently bears the torch.

text.jp:
水神様が守ってくださるはずなのに……。
どうして街に魔物が……？
text.official_en: Isn’t the God of Water supposed to keep us safe? Why are monsters overrunning our fair city?
text.real_en:
The God of Water is supposed to protect us...
Then why are there monsters in the city?

text.jp:
水神様は古くからこの国を守ってくれる
優しい神様なんですよ。
text.official_en: She is a kind and caring deity who has guarded our home since time immemorial.

text.jp:
水神様や守り人様に頼るのが
当たり前になり過ぎていたのかもしれませんね。
text.official_en: It would seem we’ve been relying too much on the God of Water and the Wardens.
text.real_en: Maybe we'd become too used to relying on the God of Water and the Warden of Water.

text.jp:
洗練された街に相応しい
選び抜かれた品々はいかがですか？
text.official_en: My products are carefully selected, as you’d expect in a city as refined as ours.

text.jp:
洪水が収まってよかったですねって。
次は笑顔を見れるように頑張るぞ！
text.official_en: She said she was glad that the water levels had gone down. I hope I get to see her smile next time!
text.real_en: She said she was glad the flood had subsided. Next time, I'll do my best to get a smile out of her!

text.jp:
流されてしまった……
あの人との思い出もすべて……。
text.official_en: It was washed away...along with all my memories of him...

text.jp: 海の発展は、オルデリオンの願いでもあるのさ。
text.official_en: After all, we’re invested in promoting maritime travel wherever we can.

text.jp:
清らかな水で育てられた野菜も
シャキッとしてて美味しいんだよなぁ。
text.official_en: But we also cultivate succulent vegetables, grown with the purest water around!
text.real_en: But the vegetables grown in our pure water are crisp and delicious, too!

text.jp:
潮風にさらされてもサビひとつないのが
うちの武器の自慢です。
text.official_en: I’m proud to say that my weapons never rust, even after long exposure to the salty winds.

text.jp: 皆、混乱しているな……。
text.official_en: The whole city’s in a panic...

text.jp:
皆さんには、水神様も守り人様も……
我々オルデリオン兵もついています。
text.official_en: The God of Water, the Wardens, and we soldiers are all here to keep you safe.
text.real_en:
The God of Water, the Warden,
and we soldiers of Olderion
are all here to stand by you.

text.jp:
知らない男の子が血相を変えて話しかけてきたの。
無事で良かったって……。
text.official_en: Next thing I knew, some strange man walked up to me with a face as red as a tomato and mumbled something about being glad I was all right.
text.real_en: A boy I didn't know came up to me looking terribly distressed. He said he was glad I was safe...

text.jp:
私も、海に出たまま帰らない人を
待つばかりじゃなくて、前を向こうと思うの。
text.official_en: Maybe I should look to the future, too...instead of waiting forever for one lost at sea.
text.real_en: I think I'll try to move forward too, instead of just waiting for the person who went out to sea and hasn't returned.

text.jp:
美しく磨きあげられた防具は
その分、身を守ってくれるんですよ。
text.official_en: The more polished a piece of armor, the better defense it provides.

text.jp:
聞いてくれよ！
橋の上のあの娘が話かけてきたんだ！
text.official_en: I have great news! The girl on the bridge came up and talked to me!

text.jp:
舟に身を任せれば、いつの間にか目的地さ。
乗っていくかい？
text.official_en: How about a ride? Sit back, relax, and you’ll be at your destination before you know it.

text.jp:
良かった……！
息子が無事で本当によかった！
text.official_en: Thank goodness! I’m so relieved my son is safe!

text.jp:
街が水没だなんて……
水神様は……。
text.official_en: A flood in our city? But surely the God of Water will...
text.real_en:
The city’s flooded...?
But the God of Water...

text.jp: 街の復興は、私たちの手で成し遂げてみせますよ。
text.official_en: But just watch! We’ll rebuild this city with our own hands!

text.jp:
街の間を舟で抜けるなんて、ここでしか味わえないよ。
乗っていくかい？
text.official_en: This is the only city in the world you can navigate by boat, you know. So how about taking a ride?
text.real_en: You can only experience a boat ride through the city here. Want to hop aboard?

text.jp:
避難した人々の住まいの確保が完了したんです。
中にはアムールに移り住んだ方もいますが……。
text.official_en: We’ve finished securing living arrangements for the evacuated citizens. Unfortunately, some had to be moved temporarily to Amore.
text.real_en: We've found places for the evacuees to live. Some have even moved to Amore...

text.jp:
避難中の人たちの寝る場所や食料の確保も
我々兵士の仕事です。
text.official_en: It’s our job to secure provisions and shelter for the townspeople who are evacuating.

text.jp:
魔物の襲撃があったって聞いてさ……
いてもたってもいられなくて
橋の上のあの娘に話しかけちゃったんだ。
text.official_en: When I heard there was a monster attack, I just knew I’d regret it if I didn’t talk to her. So I mustered up the courage and went to see the girl on the bridge!

text.jp: 魔物の襲撃があったんですってね……。
text.official_en: I heard there was a monster attack.

text.jp:
魔物の襲撃で人々が避難していたおかげで
洪水の被害は最小限だったようだね。
text.official_en: Thankfully, everyone had evacuated due to the monster attack. So the flood didn’t cause many casualties.
text.real_en: Thanks to people evacuating during the monster attack, the damage from the flood seems to have been minimal.

text.jp:
魔物の襲撃といい
水の加護が弱まっているのか……？
text.official_en:
These monster attacks... Has the protection of the waters
forsaken us?
text.real_en: With the monster attacks, too... Could the waters' protection be growing weaker?

text.jp:
魔物の襲撃に、街の水没……。
たくさん大変なことがあったけど、
街の人たちは前を向いてるわ。
text.official_en: Between the monster attack and the flood, a lot of awful things have happened here. But the people of this city are keeping their heads held high.

text.jp:
魔物はともかく……
洪水なんて俺らはどうすれば……。
text.official_en: Forget the monsters... How are we supposed to protect ourselves against a flood?
